newsitem.title: USA: US corp debt issuance seen heavy amid lower rates.
newsitem.headline: US corp debt issuance seen heavy amid lower rates.

text.p: Corporate debt issuance is expected to remain heavy for the rest of the week as Hutchison Whampoa unit's $2.0 billion debt offering nears and other issuers remain ready to capitalize on lower U.S. interest rates, dealers said.
"Most people are focused on the Hutchison deal," said one syndicate source. "We haven't heard any new names so far but yesterday we had a lot of opportunistic issuance."
About $2.5 billion in straight corporate debt priced on Wednesday, with only half of the deals scheduled to come to market as issuers took advantage of cheaper financing.
Meanwhile, Hong Kong based Hutchison Whampoa Finance Ltd is slated to bring its highly anticipated $2.0 billion multi-tranche debt offering as early as today, syndicate sources said.
The deal which has met with strong demand has been upped in size twice so far this week, players said.
The $2.0 billion offering, which started out initially at $1.0 billion, has grown to include the following four tranches, dealers said.
-$750 million 10-year debt, spread talk seen between 85-90,
-$500 million 20-year debt, spread talk seen between 100-105
-$500 million 30-year debt, spread talk seen between 110-115
-$250 million 40-year, putable in 12th year, spread talk seen between 82-85 basis points.
The A3/A-plus rated offering will be jointly underwritten by Merrill Lynch & Co and Goldman Sachs & Co, dealers said.

Among other investment grade issues, HomeSide Inc unit, Homeside Lending Inc, a full service residential mortgage banking company, is expected to issue $200 million in debt via NationsBanc Capital Markets Inc, dealers said.
The Baa2/BBB rated deal is expected to consist of seven-year senior notes, they said.
On the horizon is a $2.5 billion mega debt offering from Raytheon Co which is expected to come as early as next week via Morgan Stanley, players said.
Still, players said despite the quiet tone so far in the primary market the continuation of a positive rate environment for issuers is likely to spur some surprise issuance.
"The market's still rallying but it's been quiet so far," said another syndicate source.
"However, yesterday we started out with no names and then issuers began popping in ... people are still looking for paper," he added.
One such issuer is Bear Stearns, which has unexpectedly dropped in with a $250 million five-year debt offering on its own behalf, syndicate sources said.
Unofficial price talk on the A2/A rated deal is seen between 50-52 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, sources said.
Among Wednesday's issuers, Beckton Dickinson's 30-year debentures, priced at a spread of 60 basis points tightened a touch to trade at a spread of 59 basis points.
Also, fast-food giant, McDonalds Corp's new 10-year issue held its spread, trading in the 37.5 basis points area, where it priced, players said.
GCI Inc was also slated to bring $150 million in 10-year senior notes via Salomon Brothers Inc. Price talk was in the area of 10 percent.
Also, Standard Commercial Corp was expected to sell $100 million in eight-year notes. Price talk was seen in the 9.0 percent area, sources said.
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond was up 1/32 at 102-17/32 to yield 6.43 percent.
(( -- Nancy Leinfuss, 212-859-1675 ))
